name: Volatility-managed portfolios (volatility targeting)

origin.source_title: Volatility-Managed Portfolios (NBER WP 22208, 2016; Journal of Finance 2017)

how_it_works.simple: When markets have been shaky, hold less; when they have been calm, hold more.
how_it_works.analogy: Like driving slower in fog and faster on a clear road, so the danger stays about the same.
how_it_works.precise: Scale exposure each month by c divided by last month's realized variance, with c chosen so the managed portfolio has the same unconditional volatility as the original. Because volatility is persistent but does not predict returns proportionally, this raises Sharpe ratios; Moreira and Muir show it for equity factors and the currency carry trade.

rule: At each month end, compute realized variance RV from daily returns of the past month; next month hold weight w = c / RV in the factor or index (cap the weight, for example at 2, in practice); c is set so long-run volatility matches buy and hold.
data_needed: Daily returns of the asset or factor
economic_rationale: Changes in volatility are not offset by proportional changes in expected returns, so cutting risk when volatility is high improves the risk-return trade-off (Moreira and Muir 2017).
why_it_might_fail: Cederburg et al. (2020) find that across 103 equity strategies, real-time versions generally do not beat the unmanaged portfolios out of sample, and uncapped weights imply large leverage (up to about 15x in the catalog's test).

reported_results.notes: Volatility-managed market has an annualized alpha of 4.86% and beta of 0.6 versus the market, appraisal ratio 0.33, and about a 25% increase in the buy-and-hold Sharpe ratio. The paper also reports alphas after assumed transaction costs (Table 4, not quoted here).

Arithmetic mean of monthly returns times 12; volatility is monthly standard deviation times sqrt(12); Sharpe uses excess returns; max drawdown from monthly compounding. Weight = c / previous month realized variance, uncapped, c fitted in sample to match market volatility. Unmanaged market Sharpe 0.42, max drawdown -84.7%. Maximum weight about 15.2.

reported_results.source: Harvey, Hoyle, Korgaonkar, Rattray, Sargaison and Van Hemert (2018), Man Group
reported_results.notes: Volatility targeting raises Sharpe ratios for equities and credit, has a negligible effect for bonds, currencies and commodities, and reduces extreme returns in all asset classes.

post_publication_evidence: Cederburg, O'Doherty, Wang and Yan (2020, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jfineco.2020.04.015) find out-of-sample volatility-managed versions generally earn lower Sharpe ratios than the unmanaged portfolios (abstract read via Semantic Scholar). DeMiguel, Martin-Utrera and Uppal (2024, https://doi.org/10.1111/jofi.13395) note Barroso and Detzel find they do not survive costs, but propose a conditional multifactor version that works out of sample net of costs. In the catalog's computation the managed US market underperformed buy and hold from 2016 to 2026 (Sharpe 0.61 vs 0.88).

relevance.reason: A cheap overlay that Moreira and Muir show helps the currency carry trade, so it is a natural add-on for any parity FX strategy.

research.notes: Implemented as `stocks_vol_managed` and run officially in RUN-000003, but no hypothesis doc yet, so the stage stays at 2 until one is written. RES-0015: use as a risk control for combined FX and energy books, not as a source of return.
